title: Saudi Arabia and United Arab Emirates remain resilient as growth becomes more selective
summary: E-commerce, premiumisation and evolving consumer preferences are reshaping FMCG and Tech & Durables markets across the region
thbAction: Map the news to THB's provider CRM for referral growth, patient lifecycle engagement, and multi-facility relationship management across hospital and provider networks.
contentHtml:
Dubai, UAE & KSA – Consumer markets across Saudi Arabia and the UAE continue to demonstrate resilience, with growth opportunities emerging across FMCG and Technology & Durables (T&D), although the latest data reveals an increasingly selective and competitive retail landscape. According to NielsenIQ (NIQ)'s latest State of the Nation report, covering the months ending September 2026 (MAT Q3 2026), the UAE recorded stronger overall growth, with FMCG and T&D both expanding by more than 5%, while Saudi Arabia's FMCG market remained broadly flat and T&D delivered value growth of 2.5%.

The findings highlight a fundamental shift in consumer behaviour, with shoppers becoming increasingly selective and placing greater emphasis on value, quality, convenience and product relevance. As a result, growth is becoming more concentrated among brands and categories that successfully respond to changing consumer needs.

E-commerce is reshaping the retail landscape

Digital commerce continues to emerge as a key growth engine across both markets, increasingly influencing how consumers discover, compare and purchase products. In T&D, online sales grew by 19.4% in Saudi Arabia and 18.3% in the UAE, gaining share as offline sales declined. E-commerce is also playing an increasingly important role in FMCG, with online channels accounting for more than half of grocery expenditure in Saudi Arabia.

Meanwhile, independent retail channels are gaining momentum, outperforming organised retail in T&D across both markets. In the UAE, Traditional Trade also delivered double-digit FMCG growth, demonstrating that opportunities extend beyond conventional modern retail formats.

Category growth is becoming increasingly concentrated

Despite positive overall market performance, growth varies significantly across categories. In Saudi Arabia, Petcare was the fastest-growing FMCG category, followed by Snacking, while Ambient Food led growth in the UAE, with Petcare also making a significant contribution.

Within T&D, Photo & Optics recorded leading performance across both markets, while Headsets were a key growth driver in Saudi Arabia and Media Tablets led in the UAE. Major Domestic Appliances continued to face pressure, reflecting more cautious purchasing decisions around higher-value household products.

Consumers continue to value quality, supporting premium growth

Consumers are increasingly balancing affordability with quality when making purchasing decisions. NIQ's consumer research found that 70% of shoppers across Saudi Arabia and the UAE are willing to pay more for quality products, up from 66% in 2024.

This willingness to invest in quality is reflected in T&D, where premium brands accounted for 61% of category value in Saudi Arabia and 66% in the UAE. FMCG trends, however, reveal different market dynamics: Saudi Arabia is experiencing a clear polarisation towards value and premium propositions, while the UAE maintains a more balanced growth profile across value, mainstream and premium segments.

Increasing competition puts pressure on brand differentiation

The expansion of brands and product assortments is further intensifying competition. Active T&D brands increased by 25% in Saudi Arabia and 17% in the UAE, while FMCG assortments exceeded 104,000 active SKUs in Saudi Arabia and 136,000 in the UAE.

With more products competing for shopper attention across physical and digital shelves, availability alone is no longer enough. Brands must strengthen their differentiation, optimise their assortments and ensure that their propositions are relevant to specific consumer needs and shopping occasions.

Andrey Dvoychenkov, General Manager Arabian Peninsula and Pakistan, adds, “Saudi Arabia and the UAE continue to offer significant opportunities across FMCG and Technology & Durables, but the way brands capture growth is changing. Consumers are becoming more deliberate in their spending, embracing digital channels while continuing to invest in quality when they see a clear value proposition. The winners will be those who understand these evolving needs and translate them into sharper category strategies, stronger channel execution and meaningful differentiation. Growth is still there, but it increasingly needs to be earned.”

Growth will depend on sharper execution

The latest findings reinforce that market growth alone is no longer sufficient to guarantee business success. For manufacturers, outperforming the market will require more focused investment in high-potential categories, differentiated price propositions and channel-specific strategies. For retailers, the priority will be to balance wider product choice with simpler shopping experiences, ensuring that physical and digital assortments remain relevant and easy to navigate.

As Saudi Arabia and the UAE continue to evolve, the opportunity remains substantial. However, brands and retailers that can best anticipate consumer expectations, deliver value beyond price and execute effectively across an increasingly fragmented retail ecosystem will be better positioned to secure sustainable growth.

About the report

The NIQ State of the Nation: Saudi Arabia and UAE Consumer Markets report examines FMCG and Technology & Durables performance across the two markets, drawing on the latest 12 months of data ending September 2026 (MAT Q3 2026).

Sources: NielsenIQ RMS, NielsenIQ Retail Panel, NIQ Scantrack and NielsenIQ Market Intelligence. Consumer insights based on NIQ consumer research.
